immediate_cause: The 20-second wall-clock deadline includes capture, median/PNG creation, image registration, pose/fault queries, and logging. It expires after 1-2 accepted observations, before the required third.
correction_to_earlier_explanation: Audit timestamps bracket processing plus post-measurement pose checks and event overhead, not pure vision CPU time. Pure offline measurement is much faster.
offline_result: Same stored images and validated dependencies: first measurement about 3.3 s, second 1.5 s, third 0.2 s. ECC accounts for about 2.7 s of the initial 3.3 s. Thread counts 1/4/24 and main/worker execution preserve identical results; 1 thread was slower.
uncertainty: Exact source of live-console slowdown is not isolated by current logs. Offline replay does not reproduce 14-18 s. There is no evidence that changing CPU thread count fixes it. Current images may represent plate/camera registration shift; this does not independently prove physical displacement.
recommended_next_steps: Instrument capture, fitting, post-fit controller checks, and audit durations separately in the live observation path before another hardware run.
Budget bounded stationary acquisition explicitly while retaining three fresh consistent observations, fault checks, and pose stability checks.
Resolve the measured placement discrepancy by reseating/rechecking or a separately reviewed correction; do not silently reuse the taught endpoint.
